$comment: Realising chg's tokens (docs/rules/chg.md): a token's lexemes merged (ADR 0158), the base in its citation cell, the others in their allomorphs, joined and rewritten by chg's rules (lexicons/chg/language.yaml, lexemes.yaml). The forms are Schluessel's reading with signs for what only the Arabic writes (a vowel written or not where the default says otherwise, a twin letter, a letter written and not said, the half-space as ·; the notation's `sets` and docs/rules/chg.md say which), suffixes in archiphonemes (A U D G K, Ğ for the dative) that each orthography's `spell` resolves. An allomorph marked `free` (a scribe's other spelling) is never chosen: each that holds gives the token an alternative. realise/free/* run a language of their own; realise/chg/<lexeme>/<n> is the first course token whose realisation changes without allomorph n (a free one: whose alternatives do), realise/chg/rule-* a phonology rule a token takes. Written by packages/core-cli/scripts/chg-vectors.ts from the course: regenerate them, never edit by hand.

vectors.note: A free allomorph is never the one chosen: the token's form takes the first allomorph that is not free; the free one is an alternative.
An alternative goes through the rewrite rules as the chosen form does, with the steps it took.
A free allomorph's own conditions hold where it would stand (after a voiceless consonant)...
... and where they do not, it gives no alternative: after a vowel only the free allomorph with no condition does.
The base's own free allomorph too (where its form is its own), and every combination of the places' choices, the chosen forms first.
Where a free allomorph stands, the token's other allomorphs are chosen again around it: after the free set the instrumental is tin (after a voiceless consonant), not the din chosen after sem.
A lexeme whose only allomorph is free has no form to choose.
